en.name: Rasgulla
en.summary: Rasgulla is a ball of fresh chhena curd simmered in light syrup — and rasmalai, sandesh, cham cham and rajbhog are all the same kind of thing. These are classed as short-shelf-life sweets: keep them refrigerated and eat them within 1–2 days of being made.
en.pantry: These sweets are not shelf-stable and should not be kept at room temperature. The syrup does not preserve them: the ball itself is fresh chhena, a soft, high-moisture, low-acid curd, and syrup is a wet environment, not a dry one. Mithai counters often display trays unchilled and sell yesterday's batch, so buy from somewhere with real refrigeration. Once a box is out of the fridge, follow the 2-hour rule, or 1 hour if it is above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Keep them at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, submerged in their syrup in a covered box, and eat within 1–2 days of the date they were made. That is not our estimate: chhena sweets of this family are formally classed as short-shelf-life products to be kept refrigerated and consumed within that window from the date of manufacture. Ask when the batch was made rather than when you bought it — the two are often not the same day. Lift them out with a clean spoon and do not return one to the box.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for rasgulla and freezing does not suit it. The whole appeal is a spongy curd that has drunk up syrup, and ice crystals collapse that sponge: what thaws is dense, rubbery and weeping. Canned or retort-packed rasgulla is an entirely different product, sterilised in its tin, and keeps on the shelf until opened — after which it is a refrigerated food like any other.
spoilage: Syrup that has gone cloudy, ropy or stringy.
A sour or fermented smell instead of a clean milky-sweet one.
Balls that have gone slimy on the surface or collapsed into mush.
Bubbles or fizzing in the syrup, or a bulging container.
tips: Ask for the date of manufacture, not just the purchase date.
Buy from a counter with proper chilled display.
Keep them submerged in syrup and covered.
Buy a small box; these do not wait.

faq.q: How long does rasgulla keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 1–2 days from the date it was made, at 4 °C or below and submerged in its syrup.
No. The ball is fresh chhena and the syrup is a wet, low-acid environment. It keeps the sweet moist, not safe.
There is no timeline for it and freezing ruins the sponge. Thawed rasgulla is dense and rubbery.
That is a different product, sterilised in the tin, and keeps in the cupboard until opened. After opening, refrigerate it and treat it as a fresh sweet.

zh.name: 印度奶球
zh.summary: Rasgulla 是用新鮮 chhena 凝乳搓成球、在淡糖漿裡煮熟的孟加拉甜點；rasmalai、sandesh、cham cham、rajbhog 都屬於同一類。這類甜點被歸為短效期製品：請冷藏，並在製造後 1～2 天內吃完。
zh.pantry: 這類甜點不耐常溫，不應該放在室溫。糖漿並不會保存它們：球本身是新鮮 chhena，是含水量高、酸度低的軟凝乳，而糖漿是潮濕環境而不是乾燥環境。印度甜點櫃常常把整盤放在室溫展示、也常賣前一天的貨，所以請向有確實冷藏設備的店家購買。盒子一離開冰箱，就守 2 小時原則，超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下，整顆浸在糖漿裡、加蓋保存，並在製造日起 1～2 天內吃完。這不是我們的估計：這一家族的 chhena 甜點在正式分類上就是短效期製品，要求冷藏並在製造後這個期限內食用完畢。請問店家「什麼時候做的」，而不是只看你什麼時候買的——兩者常常不是同一天。用乾淨的湯匙夾取，拿出來的不要再放回盒裡。
zh.freezer: Rasgulla 沒有冷凍期限，冷凍也不適合它。它的魅力在於吸飽糖漿的海綿狀凝乳，而冰晶會把那個海綿結構壓垮：解凍後又密又橡皮又出水。罐頭或殺菌軟袋裝的 rasgulla 是完全不同的產品，在容器內經過滅菌，開封前可以常溫保存——開封後就跟其他冷藏食品一樣。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有發酵味，而不是乾淨的奶甜香。
球體表面發黏，或整顆塌成糊狀。
tips: 詢問製造日期，不要只看購買日期。
向有確實冷藏展示櫃的店家購買。
整顆浸在糖漿裡並加蓋。
買小盒；這種甜點不會等你。

faq.q: 印度奶球冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 從製造日起 1～2 天，放 4 °C 以下並浸在糖漿中。

faq.q: 糖漿可以保存 rasgulla 嗎？
faq.a: 不行。球體是新鮮 chhena，糖漿是潮濕低酸的環境。它讓甜點保持濕潤，不是讓它安全。
沒有對應期限，而且冷凍會毀掉海綿質地。解凍後又密又橡皮。
那是另一種產品，在罐內滅菌過，開封前可常溫保存。開封後就要冷藏，並當成新鮮甜點對待。
